title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is seeing a mix of innovation and bureaucratic maneuvering this week. From funding rounds to strategic partnerships, the landscape is shifting, albeit slowly.

themes.title: Funding Flows and Startups
themes.body: Chinese startup Spark Space is making waves with its electric-pump rocket engine tests and a fresh funding round. Meanwhile, True Anomaly's Series C raise highlights the ongoing interest in space tech ventures.

themes.title: Defense Budget Adjustments
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup has added $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, signaling a continued commitment to bolstering national security in orbit. This financial boost comes at a time when hypersonic tests are slipping, underscoring the need for reliable advancements.

themes.title: Satellite Servicing Insights
themes.body: The satellite servicing economy is looking to carbon credits for inspiration, as the industry seeks sustainable models for growth. This could reshape how we think about asset management in space.

themes.title: Tech Collaborations Emerge
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up for a tactical SDA constellation bid, reflecting a trend of defense contractors consolidating resources. Similarly, Boeing's quantum protocol demonstration hints at the increasing importance of advanced technologies in future payloads.
